# OtpField

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

forms · tier 3 · beta · runs in the browser.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For a one-time code typed one character per cell: a sign-in code, a recovery code. It is
one element, Base UI's OTP field: a group of cells and one hidden input the form sends.

**The export is `OTPField`.** The folder is `otp-field`, so the generated Import block below
prints `OtpField`, which is not an export: copy this line (choice 24).

```tsx
import { OTPField } from 'topclassui'
```

```tsx
<label htmlFor="code">Verification code</label>
<OTPField id="code" name="code" aria-describedby="code-hint" />
<p id="code-hint">Six digits from your authenticator app</p>
```

**A name is required, and it lands on the first cell.** Pass `id` (for a `<label htmlFor>`)
or `aria-labelledby`; the type refuses a field with neither. `aria-label` is refused too:
Base UI drops it on the first cell on purpose. Every later cell is named by its place,
"Character 2 of 6", from `labels.otp.character` (Arabic under an Arabic provider).
`aria-describedby` goes on the first cell, and `aria-invalid` on every cell, never on the group.
A Field's control object (`id`, `name`, `required`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`) spreads
onto it as it is:

```tsx
export function Code(control: { id: string, name: string, required: boolean, 'aria-describedby': string, 'aria-invalid': boolean }) {
  return <OTPField {...control} length={6} />
}
```

**The value is a string**: `value`, `defaultValue` and `onValueChange(value, details)`, Base
UI's names. Your handler runs first, with Base UI's details, so `details.cancel()` leaves the
code as it was. `onValueComplete`, `onValueInvalid`, `autoSubmit` and `mask` are Base UI's.

**Typing** fills a cell and moves on, Backspace clears and moves back, the arrows, Home and End
move between cells, and a paste fills every cell from the focused one. The focus cannot pass
the first empty cell. **Digits** (`validationType="numeric"`, the default): ASCII,
Arabic-Indic (`٠`-`٩`) and Persian (`۰`-`۹`) digits are taken and stored as ASCII, spaces in a
paste are dropped, any other character is refused (choice 21). The cost: no `pattern`
attribute. `alpha`, `alphanumeric`, `none` and a `normalizeValue` of your own are Base UI's, as
they are. The cells take `inputmode="numeric"` and the first takes `autocomplete="one-time-code"`.

**Left to right, always.** A code reads left to right, so in an Arabic page the cells still run
left to right and ArrowLeft goes to the cell before; the group sits at the inline start, beside
its label. A Base UI `DirectionProvider` inside the field does it.

**`length`** is 6 by default and is clamped to a whole number between 1 and 12. **`groupSize`**
draws a bar after every that many cells (0, the default, draws none). Past eight items, cells and
bars together, the row breaks at whole cells, so twelve cells stay 44 px on a phone.

**The form.** With a `name`, the hidden input sends what is typed so far, a partial code too, and
`name=` when empty. `form` ties it to a form it is not inside. Before the page hydrates the form
sends the default, and the cells take typing that is not sent: hydration puts them back to the
default. **A form reset**, a reset button or a React 19 form action that settles brings the code
back to its `defaultValue` of the latest render, on screen and in the form; a controlled field
keeps its owner's value. A reset calls no `onValueChange`.

**`invalid`** sets `aria-invalid` on every cell: each line turns red and thickens. **`disabled`**
disables every cell and the hidden input, so the form sends nothing. **`readOnly`** keeps it in
the form; it has no look of its own.

**Each cell is a square of the control scale** at most (40 px at `md`), never under 24 px tall,
and 44 px tall under a finger. It gives up width where the row does not fit: on a 320 px phone
six cells are 36 px wide (choice 38). `size="custom"` draws no size: give the cells one from your
own CSS.

**The floor.** n cells need n x 24 px plus 8 px between them: 184 px for six. A parent narrower
than that breaks the row instead of scrolling the page: two six-cell fields in a grid of `1fr 1fr`
at 320 px break 4 + 2. On a phone, give a six-cell field a row of its own.

**A wrapper** takes `OTPFieldProps`. `Omit<OTPFieldProps, 'x'>` merges the two ways to name
the field into one where none is required.

### What Base UI gives

| Base UI | Here |
|---|---|
| `Root`, `Input`, `role="group"`, the keys, paste, one tab stop | as they are; one `Input` per cell |
| `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange` with `details.cancel()` | the same names; the value is held for the form reset |
| `name`, `form`, `required`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `autoSubmit`, `mask`, `autoComplete`, `onValueComplete`, `onValueInvalid` | passed through |
| `validationType="numeric"`, ASCII only | Arabic-Indic and Persian digits too, through `normalizeValue` |
| `length`, required | optional, 6, clamped to 1 to 12 |
| `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` on the group | on the cells |
| `Separator` | not used: `groupSize` draws a bar that is decoration |

**`OTPFieldSkeleton`** is the row of cells: give it the same `length`, `groupSize` and `size`.

### Not built

The drawn 2 px border as the focus mark (choice 23: the shared ring, outside the cell), cells
that hug their text, a separator as a part, a `pattern` on numeric cells, `tone`, a hover look,
a read-only look, the invalid ring that is always on.

## Import

```tsx
import { OTPField, OTPFieldSkeleton } from 'topclassui'
```

## Props

Required: `aria-labelledby` or `id`. Every other prop below is optional.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-labelledby` | **yes**, or `id` | `string` | - | The id of the visible text that names the first cell. |
| `id` | **yes**, or `aria-labelledby` | `string` | - | The id of the first cell, which a `<label htmlFor>` points at; the others are `<id>-2`, `<id>-3`. |
| `aria-describedby` | no | `string` | - | On the first cell, beside its name: the id of a hint or an error text. |
| `aria-invalid` | no | `boolean \| 'true' \| 'false' \| 'grammar' \| 'spe...` | - | On every cell; `invalid` sets it to true, and when `invalid` is off a Field's own value survives. |
| `aria-label` | no | `undefined` | - | Refused: Base UI drops it on the first cell. Name the field by `id` or `aria-labelledby`. |
| `className` | no | `string` | - | Merged last, so a consumer class wins a conflict with the group's own. |
| `groupSize` | no | `integer`, min 0, max 12 | `0` | Draws a separator after every this many cells; 0 draws none. Clamped between 0 and length. |
| `invalid` | no | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the code as wrong: sets aria-invalid on every cell, whose line turns to danger and thickens. |
| `length` | no | `integer`, min 1, max 12 | `6` | The number of cells, one character each. Clamped between 1 and 12; past eight items the row wraps. |
| `ref` | no | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` | - | The `<div role="group">` around the cells. |
| `size` | no | `xs` \| `sm` \| `md` \| `lg` \| `xl` \| `custom` | `"md"` | The control scale of each square cell and its type step; custom emits no size classes. |

Anything else on `OTPField` and `OTPFieldSkeleton` is passed to the element it draws, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
